author: Rob Loach
install_msg: Retro installed. Load it with `[p]load retro`, then attach a ROM to `[p]retro` and play, or run `[p]retro list` to see what this bot can start. The console emulators download themselves in the background on the first load, so give them a minute. Upgrading? See the README.
name: Retro
short: Play retro console games in Discord
description: Play retro console games together in Discord. Start a game by name, URL, or an attached ROM or .zip (homebrew, or one you have the rights to) and control it with buttons under the screen. Eight consoles are supported, from the Nintendo Entertainment System to the Game Boy Advance, picked automatically from the file extension, each with its own controller layout. Every press posts an animated clip of the next second of play (0.2 to 15 seconds, configurable and fractional) on one line that names the game, the console and who pressed which button (as plain text, never a ping). A press that lands while somebody else's is still being emulated is queued rather than lost, up to three deep and one per person, and the queue is shown on that same line. Undo steps back through the last eight presses so a misclick costs nothing. [p]retroreboot reboots the running game, leaving its saves on disk alone; [p]retrosleep pauses it and [p]retroend finishes with it, leaving a Resume button. [p]retro list shows what anyone can start. Games save automatically and pick up where they left off, even after the bot restarts and even after the channel has played something else: a save state restores the exact moment, the game's own in-game save is kept beside it so it survives an emulator core update, and a game a channel has moved on from keeps a Resume button for as long as its ROM is still cached. [p]retrosaves lists a channel's saved games, exports an in-game save (or a save state) as a file to keep, imports one back after checking it against the real core, drops a save state to go back to the last in-game save, or wipes a game's progress entirely. Cores download themselves and are detected automatically, their own settings can be read and changed with [p]retroset coreoptions, and the bot owner can supply their own BIOS files (a whole zip of them at once) for cores that need one. Emulated through libretro.
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores the Discord channel and message ID of each game, the ID of the member who started it, the name of the game being played, and a copy of the ROM together with its emulator save state and the game's own in-game save, so a game can be resumed later. The same details are kept for the few most recent games a channel has moved on from, so their Resume buttons keep working. Those records are deleted by the cog itself once they can no longer resume anything: when the channel or thread is deleted, when the bot leaves the server, or when the cached ROM they name is cleaned up. Deleting a record removes the member ID in it; the game's save state and in-game save are kept, because they belong to the channel rather than to any member. The clip on a game's message is an attachment on that message and is not stored anywhere else; the server display name of whoever last pressed a button appears in that message's text, as plain text that cannot notify anyone, and is not stored anywhere either; the save states the Undo button steps back through are held in memory only and are lost when the bot restarts. Members with the Manage Messages permission, whoever started a game, and the bot owner can export a copy of a game's saves into the channel, replace them with an uploaded file, or delete them. Nothing is shared with anyone automatically. Cached ROMs, save states and in-game saves are pruned automatically as a channel plays other games.
